recursive.text: The adoption pipeline treats every candidate repository as untrusted input until proven otherwise.
A frozen contract states the goal before any action happens.
The upstream snapshot is pinned to one commit and mounted read only.
The oracle directory holds acceptance tests that nobody may edit during a run.
Every command becomes an event with a policy decision recorded first.
Outputs are stored by content hash so later steps can cite them precisely.
When the first environment is destroyed a fresh container rebuilds everything from pinned inputs.
Only then can a passing result be trusted as more than an accident.
Honest failure reports are considered a correct outcome rather than an embarrassment.
The final bundle carries enough evidence for an outside reviewer to replay the whole story.

recursive.text: What does the pipeline do? It splits long documents into retrieval sized chunks. It supports offline chunking.
Does it call any external service? No, everything runs on the local CPU without network access.
It supports offline chunking. How are chunk boundaries chosen?
Sentence boundaries are preferred and long passages are split recursively. Can I replay a run later?
Yes, every run rebuilds from pinned inputs inside a fresh container. It supports offline chunking.
What about repeated sentences? Offsets must point at each occurrence separately.
The final report lists every chunk with stable identifiers.
